THE `in_flight`/`at_sea` DIVERGENCE NAMED IN THIS TICKET'S FIRST DRAFT IS SETTLED, and the settling sharpened what the door is for. Two corrections stack. (1) My draft said 'the template names `in_flight`, every real slate writes `at_sea`'. MEASURED at the /sorted pivot the same day: THE CENSUS RAN THE OTHER WAY — 29 slates wrote `in_flight` (the template's own key), 6 wrote `at_sea`, and the `at_sea` ones were the RECENT drift, following skills/saveslate/SKILL.md's prose. So the divergence was SKILL.md vs the template. (2) AKIEN RULED 2026-07-29: 'we should globally rename in_flight to at_sea, simple.' Executed the same day — the template key and 30 slates renamed, 3 prose mentions updated, and the occurrences in cairn/ (5 files, 6 lines: MAP.md:1027 plus harbor_master + web_server history/state) deliberately LEFT because they are the records that EXPLAIN the retirement; sweeping them would erase the history of the rename itself. THE FINDING THAT MATTERS TO THIS STONE: the ruling was not a fresh decision at all but a MISSED MIGRATION — `in_flight` was already retired 2026-07-25 by the build-to-the-tool naming gate ('an AVIATION word inside a nautical system — a ship is never in flight'), the sweep covered code and missed slates/, and the template kept the dead word for four days. So SKILL.md was not drifting; it was CORRECT and out-voted 29-to-6 by a schema nobody validated against. That is precisely the charter's false claim — 'the single commons emit chokepoint validates every record against the template below' — a validation that demonstrably does not fire. A hand-rename fixes the corpus once; only the door firing the schema stops the next retired word from living four days past its gate

PUBLISH CONSTRAINT (bounded, not eliminated): both roots are public on github.com/akienm, so the boundary door's push is an outward act. Bounded BY THE THREE-ROOTS LAW — class-space holds nothing private by construction; credentials, logs and instance state live in ~/.cairn. Residual risk is a stray scratch file, so the door must NAME every untracked file it absorbs in the slate rather than sweeping silently. Push is required, not optional: a local-only commit still dies with the box

filed_edges: [CORPUS] THE BOUNDARY DOOR HAS A THIRD BEHAVIOUR NOBODY HAS NAMED. Its falsifier reds on REFUSING to write a slate on a dirty tree, and reds on SILENTLY ABSORBING an untracked file it cannot account for. So on an unaccountable untracked file it must neither refuse nor absorb — which leaves a behaviour (report and write? quarantine and write? write and red?) that has not been designed.

[AKIEN] TWO ROOTS, ONE ACT — WHAT IF ONE HALF FAILS? The door measures both roots. If it commits cairn and CairnCommons as one act and the second push fails, the boundary is half-recorded, which is worse than not recorded because it LOOKS closed. Atomicity across two repos is not free and the fallback is a design decision.

SEQUENCING, RULED 2026-08-05 (2026-08-05-filters-become-sieves): this ticket adds a new build_inspector check (working_tree_clean), and the whole family is being renamed sieve -> SIEVE. The rename lands BEFORE this ticket or AFTER it, NEVER DURING — a rename mid-build is how a proof ends up pinning a name that no longer exists. Whichever order, the new check is authored under the surviving word, not migrated across it. RESOLVED 2026-08-06: the rename landed BEFORE, while this ticket sat at TICKETME with nothing in flight — which is the clause honored, not waived. working_tree_clean is therefore authored as a SIEVE from its first line, and it is born with a BAND rather than a position: its reach runs a subprocess over local git, so it derives to correlated-local and shakes after the in-hand checks. Nobody hand-places it; the derivation reads its body (ruling 2026-08-06-a-stack-of-sieves-is-a-nest).
